name: His height
title: Just the right height
line: He was not too tall and not too short, but just right. Al-Barā’ said he had never seen anything more beautiful than him!

physical.phrase: رَبْعَةً، لَيْسَ بِالطَّوِيلِ وَلا بِالْقَصِيرِ، حَسَنَ الْجِسْمِ
physical.gloss: He was of medium height, neither tall nor short. He was of handsome physique.
physical.note: Dataset English attaches “brown of color” to his hair; in the Arabic أَسْمَرَ اللَّوْنِ describes his complexion.

physical.phrase: أَطْوَلُ مِنَ الْمَرْبُوعِ، وَأَقْصَرُ مِنَ الْمُشَذَّبِ
physical.gloss: He was taller than medium-sized, and shorter than the slender giant.
He was well proportioned in physique.

physical.phrase: مَا رَأَيْتُ شَيْئًا قَطُّ أَحْسَنَ مِنْهُ
physical.gloss: I have never seen anything more beautiful than him!
physical.note: Dataset English names the narrator “Ibn Ishaq” (Arabic: Abū Isḥāq) and adds “neither curly nor lank-haired”, which is not in this Arabic.

character.line: ‘Alī said that people who saw him suddenly felt in awe of him, but anyone who got to know him loved him.

signs.title: Never looking shorter
signs.line: There is a report that when he walked with tall people, he looked taller than them. We have not found and checked its source yet.

mirror: Stand up straight in front of the mirror. Whatever your size, how can you make people glad to know you?

name: His forehead and brows
icon: two crescent arches over a glowing lamp
title: A wide, bright brow
line: His forehead was wide, and his eyebrows were long, fine arches that did not join in the middle. A light seemed to shine over him.

physical.gloss: Broad of forehead.

physical.phrase: أَزَجُّ الْحَوَاجِبِ، سَوَابِغَ فِي غَيْرِ قَرَنٍ
physical.gloss: Endowed with arched eyebrows, perfect without being conjoined.
With a vein between them that anger would cause to pulsate.
The bridge of his nose was curved. He had a light that would rise over him.
physical.note: Dataset English goes on: “someone who did not reflect on him would consider him haughty”. The Arabic أَشَمَّ describes a high-bridged nose (at a glance it looked raised), not haughtiness.

character.trait: Angry only for what is right
character.line: He never got angry for his own sake. He only became angry when something wrong was done, until it was put right.

signs.title: Sweat on a cold day
signs.line: ‘Ā’isha saw revelation come to him on a very cold day. When it was over, drops of sweat were running down his forehead.

mirror: Look at your forehead and eyebrows. When you feel cross, how can you keep your face calm?

name: His mouth
phrase: إِذَا تَكَلَّمَ رُئِيَ كَالنُّورِ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْنِ ثَنَايَاهُ
title: Light when he spoke
line: His cheeks were smooth and his mouth was wide. When he spoke, it seemed as if light came out from between his front teeth!

physical.gloss: Endowed with smooth cheeks.
A wide mouth, cleft teeth.

physical.phrase: إِذَا تَكَلَّمَ رُئِيَ كَالنُّورِ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْنِ ثَنَايَاهُ
physical.gloss: When he spoke, it seemed as if light were emerging from between his middle teeth.

character.line: ‘Alī said he was the most truthful of all people in what he said.

signs.title: ‘Alī’s sore eyes
signs.line: At Khaybar ‘Alī had sore eyes. The Prophet ﷺ put a little of his saliva on them and prayed, and they were healed at once, as if nothing had been wrong.

signs.title: Food for a thousand
signs.line: At the Battle of the Trench, Jābir had only a little food. The Prophet ﷺ put a little of his saliva in the dough and the pot and prayed for blessing. A thousand people ate, and the pot was still full!

signs.title: A baby’s first taste
signs.line: When baby ‘Abdullāh ibn al-Zubayr was born, the Prophet ﷺ chewed a date, put a little in his mouth, and prayed for blessings for him.

mirror: Say something kind to your reflection. What true words will you speak today?

name: His neck
phrase: كَأَنَّ عُنُقَهُ جِيدُ دُمْيَةٍ، فِي صَفَاءِ الْفِضَّةِ
title: Like pure silver
line: Hind said his neck was beautifully shaped and shone like pure silver. When he turned to look at someone, he turned all the way round.

physical.phrase: كَأَنَّ عُنُقَهُ جِيدُ دُمْيَةٍ، فِي صَفَاءِ الْفِضَّةِ
physical.gloss: It was as if his neck were the neck of a statue shaped in pure silver.
He was white, as if he were fashioned from silver.
When he looked around, he looked around altogether.

character.line: When he turned to someone, he turned all the way round to face them.

mirror: Turn all the way round to face the mirror. Who will you turn to and really listen to today?

name: His chest and shoulders
phrase: عَرِيضُ الصَّدْرِ، بَعِيدُ مَا بَيْنَ الْمَنْكِبَيْنِ
title: A wide chest, a big heart
line: He had a broad chest and wide shoulders. ‘Alī said he was the most generous-hearted of all people.

physical.phrase: عَرِيضُ الصَّدْرِ، بَعِيدُ مَا بَيْنَ الْمَنْكِبَيْنِ
physical.gloss: He was wide-chested, broad-shouldered.
With the stomach and the breast in even balance.
He had splendid joints and shoulder blades.

character.line: ‘Alī said he was the best of people in generosity: in Arabic, the most generous “of chest”.

signs.title: Washed with Zamzam
signs.line: The angel Jibrīl opened his chest, washed it with Zamzam water, and filled it with wisdom and faith.

signs.title: Jarīr stays on his horse
signs.line: Jarīr could not sit firmly on a horse. The Prophet ﷺ pressed his hand on Jarīr’s chest and prayed for him, and Jarīr never fell off a horse again.

mirror: Put your hand on your chest. What will you share with an open heart today?

name: His feet and walk
title: Walking as if downhill
line: His feet were so smooth that water ran off them. He walked quickly and firmly, as if going down a slope, and his Companions had to hurry to keep up!

physical.phrase: خَمْصَانُ الأَخْمَصَيْنِ، مَسِيحُ الْقَدَمَيْنِ، يَنْبُو عَنْهُمَا الْمَاءُ
physical.gloss: The hollows of his soles were deep-set. His feet were so smooth that water bounced off them.

physical.phrase: إِذَا مَشَى كَأَنَّمَا يَنْحَطُّ مِنْ صَبَبٍ
physical.gloss: When he walked, it was as if he were descending a declivity.
He would tread inclining forward and walk comfortably.
physical.note: هَوْنًا is usually understood as “gently, with calm dignity” (compare Qur’an 25:63); “comfortably” undersells it.

physical.gloss: The earth seemed to be folded up for him. We must strenuously exert ourselves, while he is not subject to any stress.

character.line: He prayed at night until his feet swelled. When asked why, he said: “Shall I not be a thankful servant?”
He let his Companions walk ahead of him, and he was the first to say salām to anyone he met.

signs.title: “Be firm, Uḥud!”
signs.line: When the mountain of Uḥud shook beneath him and his Companions, he struck it with his foot and said: “Be firm, Uḥud!”

mirror: Look down at your feet. Where will they take you to do good today, and who will you greet first?

name: The Seal
icon: a dove’s egg in a nest
phrase: بَيْنَ كَتِفَيْهِ خَاتَمُ النُّبُوَّةِ، وَهُوَ خَاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينَ
title: The Seal of Prophethood
line: Between his shoulders was a special mark, about the size of a dove’s egg, called the Seal of Prophethood. It showed that he is the last of all the prophets.

physical.phrase: بَيْنَ كَتِفَيْهِ خَاتَمُ النُّبُوَّةِ، وَهُوَ خَاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينَ
physical.gloss: Between his shoulders was the Seal of Prophethood, for he is the Seal of the Prophets.
A red swelling like the egg of the dove.
It was like the button of the bridal canopy.
physical.note: زِرّ الحَجَلة is explained two ways: the button of a canopy, or a partridge’s egg (Tirmidhi’s own gloss in his Jāmi‘ says “egg”).

physical.gloss: Intertwined hairs.

character.line: When a little boy, as-Sā’ib, was unwell, he stroked his head and prayed for blessings for him.
When ‘Abdullāh ibn Sarjis walked round behind him hoping to see the Seal, he understood and moved his cloak so he could see it.

signs.title: A sign for Salmān
signs.line: Salmān al-Fārisī looked at the Seal on his back, and then he believed in him.

signs.title: Date palms in one year
signs.line: To free Salmān, the Prophet ﷺ planted date palms, and they gave fruit in that very same year.
signs.note: Dataset English says the palms “bore their annual crop”; the Arabic مِنْ عَامِهَا means “in that same year”, which is the point of the story.

signs.title: Strong at ninety-four
signs.line: As-Sā’ib, the boy he prayed for, was still strong and straight at 94. He said he could hear and see well only because of the Prophet’s ﷺ prayer for him.

mirror: A seal means something is complete and true. What promise will you keep today?

name: His hair and beard
title: Soft waves, few white hairs
line: His hair was gently wavy, not tightly curled and not straight, and reached his earlobes. His beard was thick, and Anas counted only fourteen white hairs.

physical.phrase: لَمْ يَكُنْ بِالْجَعْدِ، وَلا بِالسَّبْطِ، كَانَ يَبْلُغُ شَعَرُهُ شَحْمَةَ أُذُنَيْهِ
physical.gloss: It was neither crisply curled nor lank. His hair used to reach the lobes of his ears.
With four braids of hair.
He was thickly bearded.

physical.phrase: مَا عَدَدْتُ فِي رَأْسِ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ وَلِحْيَتِهِ، إِلا أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ شَعَرَةً بَيْضَاءَ
physical.gloss: On his head and his beard, I counted only fourteen white hairs.

character.line: He often oiled his hair and combed his beard.
When his Companions noticed a few grey hairs, he said: “Hūd and its sister sūras have made me grey.”

signs.title: Umm Salama’s little silver box
signs.line: Umm Salama kept a few of his hairs in a small silver container. When someone was ill, people sent a cup of water to her.

signs.title: Hardly a white hair at 120
signs.line: He wiped his hand over Abū Zayd’s face and prayed for him. Abū Zayd lived to 120, with only a few white hairs on his head.
signs.note: Tirmidhi grades it ḥasan gharīb. The “120 years” is a comment by the narrator ‘Azra, not Abū Zayd himself.

mirror: Comb your hair in the mirror. How can you look neat and clean today?

name: His words
icon: a string of evenly spaced pearls
phrase: كَلامُهُ فَصْلٌ، لا فُضُولَ، وَلا تَقْصِيرَ
title: Clear, careful words
line: He spoke clearly, so anyone sitting with him could remember what he said. He never said too much or too little, and was often quiet.

physical.phrase: كَلامُهُ فَصْلٌ، لا فُضُولَ، وَلا تَقْصِيرَ
physical.gloss: His speech was concise, neither excessive nor abridged.

physical.phrase: يَتَكَلَّمُ بِكَلامٍ بَيِّنٍ فَصْلٍ، يَحْفَظُهُ مَنْ جَلَسَ إِلَيْهِ
physical.gloss: He would pause periodically, so that those who sat with him would remember what he said.
physical.note: The Arabic says “he spoke clear, distinct speech that whoever sat with him could memorise”; “pause periodically” is an interpretation.

physical.phrase: طَوِيلُ السَّكْتِ، لا يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي غَيْرِ حَاجَةٍ
physical.gloss: Prolonged in silence. He would not speak unnecessarily.

character.line: He would repeat his words three times so that everyone could understand.
He made much of every blessing, however small, and never found fault with it.

signs.title: Short words, huge meanings
signs.line: He said he was sent with jawāmi‘ al-kalim: short sayings that hold the widest meanings.

mirror: Say one kind sentence slowly and clearly to the mirror. Who needs to hear it today?

name: His smile
title: Mostly a smile
line: When he laughed, it was mostly a smile, showing teeth as white as hailstones. Nobody smiled more than he did!

physical.phrase: جُلُّ ضَحِكِهِ التَّبَسُّمُ، يَفْتَرُّ عَنْ مِثْلِ حَبِّ الْغَمَامِ
physical.gloss: Most of his laughter was in the form of a smile that revealed teeth as white as hailstones.

physical.phrase: مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا أَكْثَرَ تَبَسُّمًا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ
physical.gloss: I have not seen anyone with a more cheerful countenance than Allah’s Messenger!
physical.note: The Arabic is more direct: “I have not seen anyone who smiled more”.

character.line: Jarīr said that from the day he became Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ never once saw him without smiling at him.
character.note: Dataset English for #225 is only “Same as the above hadith” (#224, which has ضَحِكَ “laughed”); #225’s Arabic has تَبَسَّمَ “smiled”.

character.line: He laughed and explained: “Your Lord surely marvels at His servant when he says: My Lord, forgive me my sins.”

mirror: Practise a smile that reaches your eyes. Who could use one today?

name: His voice
title: A beautiful voice
line: He had a beautiful voice. He recited the Qur’an slowly and clearly, letter by letter, stretching out the long sounds.

physical.gloss: Endowed with a handsome face and a beautiful voice.
physical.note: These are the words of Qatāda (a Successor), not a Companion. Its last clause “he did not chant in a quavering tone” sits oddly beside #307, where the same verb رَجَّعَ is translated “recited in a quivering voice”.

physical.gloss: A recitation that was explained letter by letter.
With the voice drawn out over the long vowels.

physical.phrase: كُنْتُ أَسْمَعُ قِرَاءَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، بِاللَّيْلِ وَأَنَا عَلَى عَرِيشِي
physical.gloss: I used to hear the recitation of the Prophet during the night while I was on my pallet.

character.line: He paused after each verse of al-Fātiḥa, taking his time with every word.

signs.title: Heard from far away
signs.line: At Minā, the people could hear what he said even while they were sitting in their own tents.
signs.note: Arabic فَفُتِحَتْ أَسْمَاعُنَا, “our ears were opened (for us)”; dataset English “Our ears were open” loses that.

mirror: Read a few words to the mirror, slowly and clearly. How does it feel to take your time?

name: His tears
title: A tender heart
line: His eyes filled with tears when he listened to the Qur’an, and when someone he loved was dying. He called such tears a mercy.

physical.gloss: Then I saw the eyes of Allah’s Messenger bathed in tears.

physical.phrase: وَلِجَوْفِهِ أَزِيزٌ كَأَزِيزِ الْمِرْجَلِ مِنَ الْبُكَاءِ
physical.gloss: His inner body was producing a humming sound like the humming of the cauldron due to his weeping.

character.line: He asked Ibn Mas‘ūd to recite to him, saying: “I like to hear it from someone other than myself.”
When someone saw him cry, he said: “It is a mercy.”

signs.title: The palm trunk that cried
signs.line: He used to give his talks standing by a palm-tree trunk. When he moved to a new pulpit, the trunk cried like a camel, until he came down and put his hand on it.

mirror: It is okay to cry. When you feel sad, what gentle words can you say to yourself?
